data.title: Upcoming Stock Splits This Week (September 7 to September 11) – Stay Invested
data.description:
These are the upcoming stock splits for the week of September 7 to September 11, based on TipRanks' Stock Splits Calendar. A stock split boosts the number of shares an investor owns without changing the value of their total position. In other words, the same investment is simply divided into a larger number of smaller pieces.

What makes splits interesting is that the arithmetic is often the least important part. A company whose stock has climbed from $20 to $200 faces a very different set of circumstances from one whose shares have slipped from $20 toward $2. Yet, both can end up changing their share count. The first might divide its shares through a traditional split, while the second could consolidate them through a reverse split.

That means two companies appearing on the same stock-split calendar can be there for almost opposite reasons. One may be adjusting to years of share-price appreciation, while another may be trying to put some distance between its stock and an exchange's minimum-price threshold. In either case, investors wake up with a different number of shares and a different price on the screen, but essentially the same ownership stake they had the day before.

data.title: Wall Street Loves the AI Rally – But Not the Debt Financing It
data.description:
Wall Street ended a volatile week with mixed results. The Nasdaq-100 (NDX) rose 0.38%, led by strong gains in several hardware and infrastructure large caps. The S&P 500 (SPX) finished nearly flat, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJIA) declined 0.27% as weakness in consumer discretionary, health care, and energy weighed on the less tech-heavy indexes.

Rate-sensitive sectors felt the brunt of renewed rate-hike speculation after a strong jobs report further complicated the macro picture. Early in the week, markets had cheered comments from Fed Governor Christopher Waller that were widely interpreted as dovish. But Friday's data showed hiring accelerated sharply in August, with payrolls rising at nearly triple the consensus forecast. The labor market's resilience amid still-elevated inflation pushed the odds of a rate hike at the Fed's September 16 meeting to roughly 60%.

As if to hammer home the inflation risk, diesel prices hit a new record high on Friday, potentially pushing up transportation costs and rippling across a wide range of goods. UBS now expects two rate hikes this year – in September and December – while other firms remain more cautious ahead of this week's crucial consumer and wholesale inflation reports.

Promotion

AMZO: built for a short position on AMZN

At the same time, the White House is pushing the Fed in the opposite direction. President Trump has called for rate cuts, arguing that the U.S. should have "the world's lowest" rates because its credit risk is much lower than before. High rates, in his view, put America at an unfair disadvantage relative to other countries. The President threatened to stop trading with countries that run trade deficits with the U.S. if the Fed doesn't act, claiming this approach would work better than tariffs.  

The threat isn't seen as an imminent policy shift yet, but the political pressure adds to investor unease. Trump likely has the legal authority to follow through, and the economic implications would be severe for the targeted countries – while the U.S. itself could face higher near-term inflation from disrupted supply chains.

While the macro setup remains in flux, the bond market continues to show signs of stress as it struggles to absorb a flood of corporate debt. Amazon (AMZN), Alphabet (GOOGL), Meta (META), and Oracle (ORCL) issued roughly $194 billion in bonds from January through early July – about 80% more than in all of 2025. This new supply is competing for the same pool of investor capital as Treasuries, whose yields are already elevated on macro concerns, pushing rates higher still.

And the corporate issuance wave is only just getting started. AI-related capital expenditure is expected to exceed $1.1 trillion next year and could climb further. Longer term, PwC projects global data-center spending reaching tens of trillions of dollars through 2050, with the U.S. accounting for about half. That scale of investment will require massive external financing, raising the possibility that private AI-related debt could increasingly crowd out government paper.

The bulk of that capex is slated to continue flowing into hardware, with NVIDIA (NVDA) cited as a key beneficiary. But the absolute size of the AI opportunity is already enormous, and sustained investment at these levels would expand it further – the buildout requires not only new chips, switches, and cabling but ongoing replacements and upgrades. At this scale, there's room for a wide range of beneficiaries beyond any single company.

These projections may prove overly optimistic or too conservative – the uncertainty is high, as is typical in the early stages of a new secular cycle. Still, they help explain why most major firms are bullish on stocks despite volatility, high valuations, and elevated interest rates. UBS, Citi, Morgan Stanley, JPMorgan, and others have repeatedly said in recent months that they are overweight equities and would view pullbacks as opportunities to add exposure.

In short, Wall Street is happy to recommend the stocks of the companies building the future – but remains far more cautious on the actual debt those companies are issuing to pay for the buildout.
data.author: Yulia Vaiman

data.title: The Week That Was, The Week Ahead: Macro and Markets, September 6
data.description:
U.S. stocks finished Friday mixed after a stronger-than-expected August jobs report pushed Treasury yields higher and revived concerns that the Federal Reserve could raise interest rates. The Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJIA) fell 0.51% to 53,414.25, the S&P 500 (SPX) dropped 0.38% to 7,718.60, while the Nasdaq 100 (NDX) bucked the trend, rising 0.21% to 29,544.15.

For the week, the S&P 500 gained about 0.1%, and the Nasdaq 100 rose roughly 0.4%, while the Dow slipped about 0.3%.

The 10-year U.S. Treasury yield ended near 4.78%. Gold (CM:XAUUSD) finished around $4,486, while oil (CM:CL) traded near $91. Bitcoin (BTC-USD) ended close to $79,800. The VIX closed at 14.53, up 1.47% on Friday.

data.title: Gas Prices Top $4 as Oil Above $90 Puts PSX, VLO and MPC in Focus
data.description:
U.S. gasoline prices are heading into Labor Day above $4 per gallon, with GasBuddy estimating a national average of $4.03 for the holiday, above the previous Labor Day record of $3.83 set in 2012.

A mix of higher crude prices and tight fuel supply is driving the spike. Oil (CM:CL) climbed back above $90 per barrel this week as renewed U.S.-Iran fighting raised concerns about global crude shipments. At the same time, attacks on Russian refineries have tightened supplies of diesel and other refined products.

data.title: Adobe (ADBE) Earnings Preview: Only 1 of 9 Recent Analyst Calls Is a Buy
data.description:
Adobe Inc. (ADBE) heads into this week's earnings report with Wall Street showing little enthusiasm. Of the nine latest analyst calls tracked by TipRanks, only one is a Buy, while six are Holds and two are Sells. Adobe is expected to report fiscal third-quarter earnings on September 10, and the cautious analyst setup suggests investors may need more than a routine earnings beat to become more bullish on the stock.

Wall Street expects adjusted earnings of $6.08 per share, up from $5.31 a year ago. Adobe itself guided for Q3 revenue of $6.67 billion to $6.72 billion and adjusted EPS of $6.05 to $6.10.

The bigger question, however, is whether Adobe can show that its growing AI user base is turning into faster recurring revenue growth.

data.title: 'The Unwinding Is Here,' Says Top Investor About Oracle Stock
data.description:
There has been a heavy shadow looming over Oracle (NYSE:ORCL) during the past year, one that has pushed its share price down by roughly a third.

Though there's no denying the company's immense RPO, there's also no shortage of commentary (and worries) around the cost and timeframe of converting this backlog into dollars.

Among the concerns are the expanding capex. Oracle's capex for fiscal 2026 reached $55.66 billion, and it has guided for $95 billion in 2027 (although that includes between $20 and $25 billion in customer prepayments, according to company management). Meanwhile, the company has announced plans to raise $40 billion in debt and equity in 2027.

Promotion

High conviction ORCL bears now have this Tradr ETF

For the company, the unveiling of its fiscal Q1 2027 financial figures on September 10 presents another opportunity to help convince investors that it's a solid AI pick. One top investor known by the pseudonym JR Research is already bullish, and believes that the "market's mispricing is starting to unwind."

The 5-star investor, who is among the top 2% of stock pros covered by TipRanks, acknowledges the market's pessimism. And while JR agrees that the execution risks aren't "immaterial," the investor also argues that ORCL has already bottomed out at the $120 zone.

"Unless we expect even more substantive headwinds on the AI buildout necessitating larger delays or that OpenAI's attempt to return and regain market share against Anthropic falters further, I do not think that this will cause Oracle to crater back toward those levels," adds JR.

Beyond the infrastructure buildout risks, the investor also notes that Oracle's software business and multi-cloud AI database continue to deliver strong growth. That also helps mitigate some of the existing concerns, posits JR.

To JR's mind, what matters now is Oracle's ability to build out capacity, deliver it to key customers (OpenAI et al), and monetize these contracts "quickly." Converting the backlog should allow the company's free cash flow margins to expand, adds the investor.

Of course, the "silver lining" is that ORCL is still priced pessimistically, with earnings multiples sliding in below its five-year average.

"If ORCL's recovery momentum is still early, investors should capitalize and take full advantage of it right now before it advances further," sums up JR, who rates ORCL a Buy. (To watch JR's track record, click here)

Wall Street tends to agree with that approach. With 28 Buys and 4 Holds, ORCL enjoys a Strong Buy consensus rating. Its 12-month average price target of $254.68 points to gains of 60%. (See ORCL stock forecast)

data.title: Isar Aerospace Reaches Orbit, Advancing Europe's Challenge to SpaceX
data.description:
German rocket startup Isar Aerospace successfully sent its Spectrum rocket into orbit from Norway on Saturday, marking a major step in Europe's effort to build a homegrown commercial launch industry capable of competing more directly with SpaceX (SPCX).

The launch was Isar's second attempt to reach orbit after its first Spectrum flight crashed about 30 seconds after liftoff last year. Saturday's mission reached orbit after launching from Andøya Spaceport, making it the first private space mission to do so from continental Europe.

The successful flight could strengthen Europe's efforts to develop homegrown launch capacity as governments spend more on satellites, defense, and space infrastructure. Isar CEO Daniel Metzler said the mission gives Europe "sovereign access to space."

Promotion

Isar Targets Smaller Satellite Launches

Spectrum stands 28 meters tall and can carry up to 1,000 kilograms to low Earth orbit. That makes it much smaller than SpaceX's Falcon 9, but Isar says the smaller rocket could appeal to customers that want satellites placed into specific orbits rather than sharing a larger launch.

The company has also attracted significant funding. Isar raised €270 million ($313 million) earlier this year and signed a roughly €200 million contract with the European Space Agency in August to help fund launch vehicle development.

Demand is increasingly coming from defense customers. According to Isar, defense now represents about 60% of its orders as European governments increase spending on strategic space capabilities.

Isar is building a factory near Munich that could eventually produce as many as 40 rockets per year. The company says it has already booked missions through 2028, including launches for the European Space Agency and the Norwegian Space Agency.

Reaching orbit removes a major technical hurdle, but the milestone's financial value will depend on whether Isar can launch Spectrum regularly, increase production, and convert its existing order book into recurring commercial and government revenue.

data.title: Robinhood's AI Trading Push Could Drive More Trading Activity for HOOD
data.description:
Robinhood Markets (HOOD) and other retail brokerages are opening the door to a new kind of investor: AI agents that can monitor markets, choose trades, and execute them automatically. The shift could give individual investors access to strategies once reserved for quantitative funds, while potentially creating a new source of trading activity for brokerage platforms.

Robinhood, Webull (BULL), and Moomoo have introduced tools that make it easier for customers to connect accounts to AI systems such as Claude and Codex. Investors can give those agents instructions in plain language, then allow them to scan markets and place trades based on predefined rules.

For Robinhood, the key question is whether that automation leads customers to trade more often and use more advanced products. The company already keeps AI-managed portfolios in separate accounts and sends users notifications for every trade.

data.title: 'This Is For Certain,' Says Top Investor About SpaceX Stock
data.description:
There's not always agreement when it comes to companies and their valuation. SpaceX (NASDAQ:SPCX) offers yet another example of this dynamic.

Wall Street analysts, for instance, have decisively opposing viewpoints, with price targets ranging from a high of $800 to a low of $75. That's an ocean apart, and reflects the difference of opinions surrounding the company.

On the one hand, opportunity beckons. In its final roadshow pitch deck, the company outlined a $28.5 trillion total addressable market, including $22.7 trillion in enterprise applications. These are truly fantastic numbers in every sense of the word, and the company generated enormous excitement surrounding its IPO just a few months ago.

Promotion

High conviction SPCX bulls now have this Tradr ETF

However, there are plenty of challenges – technical and otherwise – that SpaceX will have to surmount in order to realize these immense markets. That will include increasing capex costs, and the company reported total capex of $18.4 billion in Q2 (the vast majority going to AI).

The risk and reward are therefore quite large, as top investor Andres Cardenal puts it succinctly:

"SpaceX is a very particular company with tremendous execution risk and exponential growth opportunities," declares the 5-star investor, who is among the top 1% of stock pros covered by TipRanks.

Cardenal notes that the company has multiple long-term growth drivers. The company's connectivity business recently experienced 65.8% revenue growth, and the investor points out that Starlink's "cash-generative model" helps to support the capital-hungry Space and AI segments.

Starship is another one. The ability to reuse and increase capacity per launch has the potential to "dramatically change the economics of the whole business." While Cardenal admits that the idea of putting data centers in space sounds like science fiction, he also argues that SpaceX is the best positioned to deliver this technology in the future.

And yet, he doesn't deny the risks and red flags, as operational risks, "gargantuan" capex, and regulatory pitfalls are all present. Cardenal therefore posits that a position size of 2% to 3% sounds about right (for him, at least).

"One thing is for sure: SpaceX will be a volatile stock, depending on how space launches go, demand for AI, and various factors related to market risk sentiment across different time periods and market cycles," concludes Cardenal, who rates SPCX a Strong Buy. (To watch Cardenal's track record, click here)

Despite the competing views, Wall Street as a whole is moderately bullish when it comes to SpaceX. With 25 Buys, 6 Holds, and 3 Sells, SPCX carries a Moderate Buy consensus rating. Its 12-month average price target of $228.04 points to gains of 54%. (See SPCX stock forecast)
